• **Conservation of Energy:**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is conserved in elastic collisions but not in inelastic collisions.
 
• In a closed system, the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) remains constant.
 
 
 
• **Relation to Work:**
 
 
• The work done by a force is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the object it acts upon.
 
• This relationship is described by the work-energy theorem.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• A moving car, where the mass and speed determine its kinetic energy.
 
• Flowing water in a river or dam, used to generate hydroelectric power.
 
• A bullet fired from a gun, where its velocity imparts significant kinetic energy.
